title: Internal or external?
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: When you reach a goal, who tells you it counts: you, or someone else?
I asked: after you reach a goal, how does it get validated in your thought process? You say: I reached it, I celebrated it. Is it all internal, or external as well?

A student said: both. You want it to be as internal as possible. I can be guilty of getting the satisfaction of the goal through external affirmation, which isn't helpful when you rely on external feedback for your own approval.

I said that another entrepreneur once told me one of the problems he realized in life was that his father never set his goals high enough. I always set my goals as moving targets, so that I could achieve, and achieve, and achieve.

As an overachiever, I said, which entrepreneurship and overachieving are very related, you have to analyze: once I reach that success, is it ninety percent internal, where I am celebrating, or is ninety percent some external force that I'm not in control of?
A student offered: maybe an addiction to solving problems, to having problems to solve.
Where does your sense that you did well come from?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the last goal you reached and how you celebrated it.
Write how much of the satisfaction was from others.
Write what you would need to feel it from the inside.
Write whether your goals are moving targets, and why.
Write what problem you keep solving so you never stop.

check.q: What did a student say you want your validation to be?
What did I ask about reaching a goal?
choices: How does it get validated: inside or outside?

check.q: What did the entrepreneur I quoted say about his goals?
choices: He set them as moving targets

recap: Know where your sense of success comes from. Be careful with moving targets.
